do_not_assume: A calendar event automatically has a registration
An instance automatically places people into a group
A selected gateway supports payment plans
goal: A configured but not yet broadly launched instance with explicit ownership of shared and event-specific settings.
steps: Define the registrant population, registrar model, required fields, cost model, capacity, group destination, communications, and follow-up owner.
Reuse an appropriate template or create one with authorized template administration.
Put reusable form, eligibility, finance, communication, workflow, signature, and placement settings on the template.
Create the instance and set its registration dates, contact, capacity, payment deadline, and any instance-owned finance settings.
Create or select the operational group if the event requires a roster or check-in.
Create or select the event item and occurrence.
Add the registration, group, campus, public name, and URL slug linkage as required.
Leave the instance inactive when the workflow requires review before publication.
Test representative free or paid, single- or multi-person, eligible and ineligible paths.
Activate only after public routing, communications, payments, placement, and permissions pass.
title: Recipe: Create a reusable registration and one event instance

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Evidence that representative costs and payment paths produce the intended registration and financial state.
steps: Confirm whether cost is owned by the template or instance.
Verify the financial account and gateway.
Test base cost, every required or optional fee used by the event, and representative discounts.
If partial payments are enabled, test the minimum initial payment and default amount.
If payment plans are enabled, verify provider compatibility and inspect the plan at the gateway.
Confirm payment, total cost, balance, fees, and discounts on the registration.
Test confirmation and payment-reminder communications.
Test an authorized manual payment and refund in a safe environment or approved reversible scenario.
Document how post-registration balance changes will be reconciled with gateway schedules.
Stop before launch if Rock and the gateway disagree.
title: Recipe: Validate a paid registration before launch

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The person becomes a complete, paid-as-required registrant with the intended group membership.
steps: Confirm available capacity and identify the exact wait-listed registrant.
Move that registrant from the Wait List tab.
Send the completion email unless a reviewed alternative follow-up is in place.
Confirm the person opens the correct registration.
Collect any payment and questions omitted during wait-list entry.
Verify the full-registration status.
Verify configured group membership and any required Group Member Attributes.
Reconcile capacity and the remaining wait-list order.
Stop when the registrant is complete across status, data, finance, and group placement.
Confirm the registrant is now marked as a full registrant.
Confirm that configured group placement occurred.
Verify whether the move email was sent.
Open its completion link as a test recipient and confirm it requests payment and fields omitted during wait-list entry.
Check whether the person completed that follow-up flow.
If payment completion fails, compare the installed version with the supplied v19.3 fix.
Stop when status, required data, payment, and group placement all reconcile.
title: Recipe: Promote a wait-listed person to full registration

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Every published metric has an explicit grain, population, and reconciliation test.
steps: Inventory all metrics and label their grain.
Define confirmed, wait-listed, canceled, and other local populations.
Trace a multi-person registration through registration-level and registrant-level metrics.
Trace a wait-listed person through every chart.
Reconcile fee, payment, discount, and balance metrics separately.
Document local sources and precedence for staff, serving, or department segments.
Mark overlapping dimensions as non-additive.
If comparing events, align them by the chosen lifecycle stage.
Restrict participant drilldowns to the intended staff audience.
Stop publication if a metric cannot be reconciled or its local truth source cannot be validated.
title: Recipe: Audit an event-registration dashboard

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A family can preregister without unnecessary friction, records are usable at check-in, and staff receive an owned follow-up action.
steps: State the benefit to the family on the public page.
Define how adults, children, families, aliases, and existing records will be resolved.
Minimize duplicate and partial record creation.
Define the workflow or connection process that receives the submission.
Assign an owner and expected follow-up state.
Test a new family, an existing family, a partial submission, and likely duplicate inputs.
Confirm family records and child data are usable by the intended check-in configuration.
Confirm the workflow or connection request appears with the intended person, campus, and reviewed attributes.
Confirm staff can complete the follow-up without relying on private troubleshooting data.
Stop broad launch if record quality, check-in eligibility, or follow-up ownership is unresolved.
title: Recipe: Launch family preregistration with follow-up
